title: New tap by Lawrence and Hale, and Bubbles' restrictions on Green
summary: Green says Lawrence and Hale kept introducing new works and Hale was self-taught, while Green himself was held back by Bubbles' orders to avoid celebrity.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: So what was happening with the kind of tap dancing that was going on at this particular time? What was Baby Lawrence and Teddy Hale -- what kind of tap dancing were they doing in relationship to the music? How were they changing tap dancing or was it just the same as it always had been?
No, it wasn't the same as it always had been. Because they kept introducing new works, you see? They reinstating, you see, they'd reinstate it, once they -- like

what they call repertoire. Or medley, see a medley is more than -- it's at least about three or four different songs. And they're melodies, you see? So, the tap dancer's dream, like Baby Lawrence, especially, they just -- Teddy Hale, see now he -- like the bolero, see that was introduced into the jazz media. By this -- this Eddie Haywood's son, Hayward's song, I think. You see. Eddie Haywood, Jr., he did this -- he gave some kind of beat to the Bolero -- which appealed to Teddy Hale, personage, you know, you see.

But he didn't always do his tap dance to that. He was like what you call self-taught. You know, like once they acquire the ability a person has a tendency to use different motives for emotions, you know. It's -- I think it's romancing the art itself, see. Which he was great at, you see, now I'm his teacher, you see, but I just taught him, cause he asked me to, you see? I could understand that, see? But I wasn't allowed to adopt anyone at the time, see, I was under special contract and I was only allowed to do certain things, I had to follow orders. Understand?
Whose orders were you following then?
That was John Bubbles, Buck and Bubbles.
Were you under contract with -- who was Teddy Hale under contract with?
Well I really didn't -- I never found that out, I mean he was originally under contract with Ted Lewis,
you see? The "Me and My Shadow", maestro, bandleader. See?
And what sort of restrictions was John Bubbles placing on you, at the time?

Well that I couldn't -- I wasn't allowed to go back and be a celebrity at all times. I had to be, you know, couldn't be -- have to be careful with exposing one's career. You understand? Like, if you're -- if you're appearing in a place and someone know that you are popular, or it gets -- the word gets backstage they will -- show folk had a tendency to -- you'd either have to get up and take a bow, and sometime the audiences, you know, it'd be fan clubs in them audiences, you see? And they would insist that you get up, if the audience don't do it, the master of ceremonies or whoever they are, you know, would insist on it, maybe the manager or the owner of the -- I mean the place, that's -- you get lectured, you know, by your elders.
So Bubbles told you what in confidence?
